The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) locked down the entire US-Mexico border airspace to drones through 2027 to counter cartel threats, restricting unauthorized drone operations in the region [FAA locks down entire US-Mexico border airspace](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiogFBVV95cUxNdDg1dDI4Mm9ZVWhPUWc5RWxadlR5dFZHR0JENjU5QmVXRDBSVWJmTGxidzJqYXVheTQzeEJVLUtST0lVeHFtaDJkRVBrcVI5bExHRTg5M3FNSGF0REtOb0o5S3dERk42OUoxZWFqdFVaemkxclh2US1HaHVLblE2ZjBvenVkRHFKckJwZGNNQ2pySXd0TVUtbjh4akhPVUJiRlE). This action reflects a broader trend of increased federal oversight of autonomous and unmanned systems.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is intensifying its scrutiny of autonomous vehicles, auditing 1,000 Tesla Cybercabs [NHTSA Audits 1,000 Cybercabs](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiggFBVV95cUxQbXJHT3o3VURFQWw1YlI0cVBnSDY3TFhCYkxVOV9NUzk2UlltbFg3UE9iY2pZU0gtY0w1ZnZpRlVvOHhEYVVYamdmNWhwMTBubjBWeGVndjBockMzSndFY2o5d2ZPaW1QcGt0YWhQUlZGWC1OSkRMSjRlRnRvZEJ2Q2Fn?oc=5) and opening a probe into Robotaxis for speeding and ignoring school zones [NHTSA Opens Probe](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMic0FVX3lxTE8zQThsSmRPZXVoOHRjRmt6QllXU1lQYkJuQ0o1ckdVX2lDbmg0Nk4yTnlyamxqU0lnanc2Qk1sdVJZMlFRUE1BN1lwSFZiVzl3U2NBWFBWN1I5VDA4cEZFUHBEdkNYb1JhLS0xbmtCNlduQ1E?oc=5). Meanwhile, Tesla targets 2026 for Cybercab sales.

In aviation, the FAA issued certification for the Boeing 737 MAX-10 [FAA issued certification](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/federal-aviation-administration-issues-certification-boeing-737-max-10) and announced the first-ever Special Airworthiness Market Survey Certificate for eVTOL aircraft [Secretary Sean P. Duffy Announces](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-announces-first-ever-special-airworthiness). The agency also proposed a $351,000 civil penalty against Creamer Pilot Services for alleged unauthorized passenger-carrying operations [FAA proposes $351,000 fine](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/faa-proposes-351000-fine-against-creamer-pilot-services-alleged-unauthorized-passenger).

Regarding ground transport, the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration finalized a decision to renew and modify an hours-of-service exemption for the Association of American Railroads and the American Short Line and Regional Railroad Association [FMCSA announces final decision](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/21/2026-21488/hours-of-service-of-drivers-association-of-american-railroads-and-american-short-line-and-regional). Additionally, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration proposes to conduct a new Older Novice Driver Study [NHTSA proposes new study](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21264/agency-information-collection-activities-submission-to-the-office-of-management-and-budget-for).
